source.title: The Evaluation Game: Beyond Static LLM Benchmarking
source.authors: Paul Wang; Jade Garcia Bourrée; A. Kermarrec; Vincent Corruble

record.tranche_reason: Extends empirical study of safety fine-tuning by measuring how refusal transfer varies with prompt-to-training-set embedding distance. It does not test the specified token-position or bypass claims.
record.gate_note: The paper measures refusal rates after fine-tuning on adversarial-harmful prompts and finds distance-dependent transfer. That is related to safety fine-tuning, but none of V1–V7 names prompt-embedding-distance locality. The experiments do not test fine-tuning that induces compliance, benign-data fine-tuning, per-token KL, opening-token or attack bypasses, safety-localized parameters, causes of token-depth shallowness, or deepening safety. Prompt-transformation operator results and cited findings from other work are not claim rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes instruct models on adversarial-harmful prompts paired with refusal training and measures how increased refusal transfers by embedding distance. It does not induce harmful compliance, use benign data, measure per-token KL, test prefill/suffix/decoding bypasses, localize safety in parameters, explain shallowness, or test deepening. It cites the original sources only in related work. The reader's 'tests/T3' label is wrong because no result bears on any version V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: authors conclude that refusal fine-tuning on adversarial prompts induces only local, distance-dependent generalization across Llama, Mistral and Qwen, supporting their ε-coverage assumption, and that prompt transformations behave approximately like group actions in embedding space. They also argue static benchmarks cannot distinguish genuine fixes from memorized patches.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA refusal training on a shared 47-prompt adversarial-harmful pool and measures refusal rates by prompt embedding distance. It does not apply the original sources’ harmful-compliance fine-tuning, token-position KL measurement, or compliant-prefix bypass methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Distance-dependence strength varies substantially by embedding pooling metric: spectral_all has ∆WAICnull ≥ 2,000 in every main cell, while mean_pool can be as low as +6.7. The direction indicator is near indifference for Qwen rank 2 at mean_pool (0.551). Results also vary by model and LoRA exposure/rank.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-oriented LoRA fine-tuning on 47 adversarial-harmful prompts raises held-out refusal (e.g. Llama 0.299→0.808), with the fine-tuned refusal rate decreasing with embedding distance to the training prompts in 17/18 cell×metric entries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety (refusal) fine-tuning on discovered jailbreaks generalizes locally, with weaker transfer to prompts far in embedding space from the training set.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-rate gain after refusal fine-tuning depends on model family and exposure budget (Mistral widest range, Qwen near zero until exposure 800).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dose-response of refusal fine-tuning varies by model family and exposure.

record.problems: The fine-tuning generalization experiment uses three relatively small fine-tuned models, one judge model, and prompt-prompt distances computed in base-model embedding spaces; the authors note downstream conclusions may depend on these choices. The main reported fits use one training-stochasticity seed. The paper reports model-averaged evidence and credible intervals, but no uncertainty bars for the empirical refusal-rate means in Table 2.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted from the reported distance-transfer and dose-response results. Prompt-transformation operator-fit and algebraic-coherence experiments are outside the claim; cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning to induce harmful compliance; training raises refusal.
No benign-data fine-tuning measured for harmful compliance (vanilla_benign used only for over-refusal).
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No parameter localization of safety (LoRA rank is a training setting, not a localization test).
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No deepening method trained or evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to 'none'. Relation downgraded from tests/T3 to cites_only/T6: Qi et al. (both originals) appear only as citations in related work. The fine-tuning increases refusal (defensive), the opposite direction from V1's harmful-compliance fine-tuning, so it neither supports nor challenges V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune harmful examples to induce compliance or measure harmful compliance as the claimed effect; fine-tuning is described as refusal training.
Does not fine-tune on ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data and measure resulting harmful compliance.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence or compare aligned and base output distributions across response positions.
Does not test compliant-prefix prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as refusal bypasses.
Does not locate safety behavior in a small set of weights or ranks.
Measures refusal transfer by prompt embedding distance, not why safety behavior would be shallow across response tokens.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens.

rows.subject: L LAMA-3.1-8B-I NSTRUCT
rows.operation_detail: LoRA fine-tuning on 47 adversarial-harmful prompts, cycled to exposure 1600; rank 1

conditions.value: 2999 held-out prompts; ncell=2876 after ambiguous-only pairwise drops

rows.measure: Empirical refusal rate and its dependence on normalized embedding distance to the training pool
rows.value: Fine-tuned refusal rate 0.808; rate difference +0.509; ∆WAICnull +738; P(z-dep) > 1 − 10−6; best shape CPL; P(pft(1)<pft(0)) > 1 − 10−6
rows.uncertainty: Posterior probabilities reported; no error bar for the empirical rates stated in this table
rows.note: Outcome is increased refusal after refusal training, not increased harmful compliance. The authors report distance dependence.
